title: Classify two-prime phase blocks and prove capacity invariance
body:
**Alphabet reduction and block classification:** for every pair of distinct odd primes p<q and positive a,b, the maximum number of orthogonal columns with p+q entries is the same over mu_(p^a q^b) as over mu_(pq). Higher prime powers cannot increase this exact capacity. Every matrix that cannot descend has at most p columns and splits, after row permutation and phase changes, into a p-row mu_p block and a q-row mu_q block with relative column phases. **No new kappa** or physical supplier follows.

Read the [universal proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/316768a3497a88c17fca54cf5d5b240b2ea0b959/research/odd-prime-phase-blocks/PROOF.md), [exact certificates](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/316768a3497a88c17fca54cf5d5b240b2ea0b959/research/odd-prime-phase-blocks/RESULT.json), [checker](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/316768a3497a88c17fca54cf5d5b240b2ea0b959/research/odd-prime-phase-blocks/verify.py), [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/316768a3497a88c17fca54cf5d5b240b2ea0b959/research/odd-prime-phase-blocks/SOURCE-PINS.json) and [credits](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/316768a3497a88c17fca54cf5d5b240b2ea0b959/research/odd-prime-phase-blocks/CREDITS.md). This extends [PR #7775](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7775)'s p=3 theorem with a product invariant that works for every odd prime.

| Result | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| Capacity equality | p+q rows; p<q distinct odd primes; all positive prime powers |
| Essential-phase normal form | `[A D; B]`, with orthogonal columns in A over mu_p and B over mu_q |
| Descent threshold | Every matrix with at least p+1 columns descends to mu_(pq) |
| Sharpness | p-column counterexamples for every alphabet larger than mu_(pq) |

Lam and Leung's classical cycle theorem makes each pairwise zero sum one p-cycle plus one q-cycle. Quotient phases force one common p-row subset. For two columns in the same phase class, ratios to a third class give two permutations of a prime cycle. Their product invariant prevents replacing one root of that cycle by a different root. Thus the column restrictions are orthogonal on both blocks. Dimension gives at most p columns, and phase normalization gives the stated block form. A stacked Fourier construction attains p columns already in the smaller alphabet, which completes the capacity equality. The actual squarefree capacity remains unknown here except for the retained eight-row result.

Python 3.12 and the standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/odd-prime-phase-blocks
```

Both modes print:

```text
PASS_ODD_PRIME_PHASE_BLOCKS
General two-block classification, sharp p-column boundary and prime-power capacity equality
Exact quotient, relative-permutation, cycle-product, phase-gauge and mutation checks pass
Unchanged p=3 descent and complete eight-row capacity sources pass
```

Exact checks cover 82,728 canonical quotient cases and 1,252,944 full subset cases for five-row subsets of twelve rows in Z/3. The latter tests the odd-group combinatorial lemma beyond the root quotients for primes 5 and 7. All 5,166 relative permutations for p=3,5,7 are checked; they represent arbitrary permutation pairs up to a common row permutation. The checker covers all 82,906 rotated cycle pairs in twelve stated alphabets, 124,766 relevant product submultisets, 3,448 recorded Gram entries, explicit same-class examples and 24 single-entry mutants. A p=2 example demonstrates failure of the product implication outside the odd-prime hypothesis. These are finite controls for the written universal proof, not an enumeration of all matrices.

All 37 retained files are authenticated. The complete p=3 verifier and its nested eight-row capacity certificate run unchanged. Normal/optimized registered checks, syntax/indentation, committed bytes/source history/modes, export and sealed read-only Git-free serial replay pass. Hosted CI did not certify this package. The [plan job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/44454367748/job/135325684914) failed in the shared `test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record`: the base guide names frontier6030 while the selected record requires `make frontier7000-verify`. The log reports 760 tests, one failure and 24 skipped; package replay was skipped. This package changes no shared CI file. Local replay remains the scientific evidence.

Ali Romman (@aliromman) supplied [PR #7775](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7775)'s [p=3 proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/00daa049c349349f7db27ae7ddaf2f56116aaf79/research/two-prime-alphabet-descent/PROOF.md), [certificate](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/00daa049c349349f7db27ae7ddaf2f56116aaf79/research/two-prime-alphabet-descent/RESULT.json) and [checker](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/00daa049c349349f7db27ae7ddaf2f56116aaf79/research/two-prime-alphabet-descent/verify.py). Nick Petalas (@petalas) supplied [PR #7744](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7744)'s [two-prime completion question](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7dc85513e8ee9b771a5856f027cf199936f85af0/research/two-prime-column-completion/README.md). T. Y. Lam and K. H. Leung supplied the classical input in [On Vanishing Sums of Roots of Unity, Corollary 3.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9511209#page=8). All predecessor notices remain intact; no global literature priority is claimed.

The squarefree optimization, classification of the smaller blocks, even-prime cases, a third prime divisor, other row counts, approximate orthogonality, native realization and complete caller costs remain outside this result. No selected cold replay, Lean, Docker, independent human or formal-kernel acceptance is claimed. All five framework assumptions and the selected frontier remain unchanged.
